steps.title: new inside send()
steps.caption: send() picks the channel with if/else, so Notifier knows every channel and push means another edit.
steps.body: `Notifier.send(msg, kind)` decides which channel to build with an if/else on `kind`, and calls `new` on each concrete class itself. Notifier now depends on `EmailChannel` and `SmsChannel` directly, so adding push means opening `send()` again, adding a branch and retesting a method that every caller uses.

steps.title: Defer to createChannel()
steps.caption: send() calls createChannel() and talks only to Channel; each subclass returns its own channel.
steps.body: `send()` asks `this.createChannel()` for a channel and uses it only through the `Channel` interface. `createChannel()` is the **factory method**: `Notifier` (the *Creator*) declares it, and each *ConcreteCreator* overrides it to return its own *ConcreteProduct*. That gives two parallel hierarchies, and `send()` is written once.

steps.title: One call at runtime
steps.caption: send() runs in the base class; createChannel() runs in SmsNotifier and returns a new SmsChannel.
steps.body: The client calls `send('Your code is 4721')` on an `SmsNotifier`. The inherited `send()` runs, `this.createChannel()` is dispatched to `SmsNotifier`, which returns a new `SmsChannel`, and `send()` then calls `deliver(msg)` on it through the `Channel` interface. The result, `SMS sent: Your code is 4721`, travels back to the client.

steps.title: New channel, no edits
steps.caption: Push adds two classes and edits none: send() is untouched. The cost: a creator subclass per product.
steps.body: Push needs a `PushChannel` and a `PushNotifier` that creates it, and no existing class changes: `send()` is untouched. Java's `Collection.iterator()` works the same way, with each collection class creating its own iterator. The price is a creator subclass for every product, which is why many languages pass a factory function instead.

references.title: Gamma, Helm, Johnson and Vlissides — Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software (1994)
Joshua Bloch — Effective Java, 3rd edition (Item 1, static factory methods)
Martin Fowler — Replace Constructor with Factory Function
